sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)
ordered surface loop (10 aa): pLDDT>=70, DSSP loop/turn, exposed junction residue (max RSA), indel-tolerant, 3D-clear of features

literature_notes: All seven ledger lines (L1–L7) describe the same two constructs: GFP-RhBG (GFP fused to the N-terminus) and RhBG-GFP (GFP fused to the C-terminus) of full-length human RhBG expressed in MDCKI cells or C2C12 myotubes. The authoritative topology landmarks place the N-terminus (residues 1–14) in the INTRACELLULAR compartment and the C-terminus (residues 416–458) also in the INTRACELLULAR compartment. Therefore both GFP fusions face the cytoplasm; neither constitutes an extracellular surface tag. The papers confirm that the tagged protein traffics correctly to the plasma membrane, but the GFP moiety is not on the extracellular face in either construct. No ledger line reports a tag insertion in any extracellular loop or at an extracellular terminus of RhBG or a close ortholog. The six extracellular loops (ECL1 35–61, ECL2 108–124, ECL3 173–179, ECL4 241–251, ECL5 304–306, ECL6 365–394) are topologically accessible but are not supported by any ledger-grounded insertion. Zero extracellular tag sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: GFP-RhBG N-terminal GFP fusion: the N-terminus (residues 1–14) is intracellular per topology landmarks; tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface, though the protein traffics correctly to the plasma membrane.

RhBG-GFP C-terminal GFP fusion: the C-terminus (residues 416–458) is intracellular per topology landmarks; tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface, though apical and basolateral membrane localization is preserved.
